question.leadin: In July 1990, this country was accused of slant drilling into the Rumaila oil field; a month later, this country was invaded.
question.text: Name this Middle Eastern country. American forces supported this occupied country during the First Gulf War.
question.clue: This nation lacks any permanent rivers, and depends on desalination plants to provide drinking water for its inhabitants.

swap.leadin: The Rashidun caliphate spread Islam throughout much of the Middle East.
swap.text: The caliphate was mostly composed of tribes of this ethnic group. Egypt, Iraq, and Algeria have large populations of this ethnic group, for which the peninsula containing Oman and Yemen is also named.
swap.clue: An emperor of this ethnicityheld theSecular Games on the thousandth anniversary of Rome's founding but was overthrown and killed by Decius ("DEE-shuss").

question.leadin: British possessions in Asia were referred to as "East of" this structure.
question.text: Name this waterway that connected the Mediterrainian and Red Sea when it was completed in 1869.
question.clue: The Straits of Tiran were opened during a conflict over this structure that led to Anthony Eden's resignation.

swap.text: A second oil shock occurred in 1979, partially due to this country's regime change and a subsequent war with Iraq. Shah Mohammed Reza Pahlavi was deposed as leader of this country by the Ayatollah Khomeini.
swap.clue: This country was led by Mohammad Mosaddegh, and this nation's Qajar dynasty was replaced by its Pahlavi dynasty.

question.leadin: Name these groups fighting in Syria.
question.text: Over the latter half of 2017, this group lost much of its territory, after being ousted from Raqqa. This organization declared its caliphate in 2014 in Mosul.
question.answerHtml: ISIS [accept ISIL, Daesh, and the Islamic State of Iraq and Syria]
question.clue: Brett McGurk is the American special envoy to a coalition against this group.

swap.leadin: Saif ad-Din Qutuz, a member of this military caste, crushed the Seventh Crusade and later defeated a Mongol army at the Battle of Ain Jalut.
swap.text: Name these enslaved Muslim warriors who wielded great power throughout North Africa and the Middle East.
swap.clue: They followed the furusiyya code, which includes cavalry tactics and horsemanship.

question.leadin: In one episode of this empire's history, Sitt al-Mulk ordered the death of two heirs, resulting in the ascension of Al-Zahir.
question.text: Name this Shia empire based out of modern day Egypt and named for the daughter of Muhammad. It flourished in the 10th century until its eventual decline and conquest by Saladin in 1171.
question.clue: That "mad" ruler from this dynasty, al-Hakim, mysteriously disappeared on one of his meditative night walks and is venerated by the Druze.

swap.leadin: This super-secret document was revealed by the Bolsheviks in a 1917 issue of Pravda.
swap.text: Name this 1916 document signed by Imperial Russia, Britain, and France, which divided up the lands of the Ottoman Empire into "spheres of influence."
swap.clue: It was supplemented by the Agreement of Saint-Jean-de-Maurienne and it was modified at the Conference of San Remo.

question.text: Breaking an Egyptian blockade on the Gulf of Aqaba, Israel took the Sinai Peninsula, Golan Heights, and West Bank in this brief 1967 skirmish.
question.clue: At the beginning of this war, one side immediately destroyed over half the air force of another in Operation Focus.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about medieval mapmaking.
swap.text: This city's Balkhi school of geography produced many maps in the T and O style. An apocryphal account describes how a river in this city ran black with ink from the maps and books destroyed during a Mongol siege.
swap.clue: After one event in this city, a river supposedly ran black with ink and its ruler was trampled in a carpet.

question.text: Ahmad Sanjar, a later Seljuk Turk ruler, fought campaigns against these Ismaili Muslims whose name now describes their common action of covertly killing rulers they didn't like.

swap.text: This leader, who lost the Toyota War, personally designed a car with a rocket-shaped nose and tail. Under this leader, his country's flag consisted of a single shade of green.
swap.answerHtml: Muammar Gaddafi [or Muammar Qaddafi or Muammar al-Gaddafi or Muammar Muhammad Abu Minyar al-Gaddafi]
swap.clue: This leader changed his country's flag to a pure green banner and set out his ideas in the Green Book.

question.leadin: In the United States, the names of certain foods are often changed due to foreign policy.
question.text: Bob Ney renamed French fries to "freedom fries" due to French opposition to this U.S. action, which Michael Ledeen argued was justified due to a dictator's purchases of yellowcake uranium from Niger.
question.answerHtml: invading Iraq [or descriptive answers indicating war with Iraq; or the Iraq War; or Operation Iraqi Freedom; or the Second Gulf War; or Second Persian Gulf War; prompt on Gulf War or Persian Gulf War]

swap.leadin: The second of these events was triggered when Ariel Sharon visited the Al-Aqsa mosque.
swap.text: Give this word, which translates to "shaking off," that commonly refers to two violent Palestinian uprisings in 1987 and 2000.
swap.clue: An early attempt to end that one of these events was the Sharm al-Sheikh agreement, and during it the UN announced a Road Map to Peace.

question.leadin: Percy Cox met this man at Hasa Oasis in 1917 and pressed the British case for an alliance with this ruler against Mark Sykes' support for Sharif Hussein.
question.text: Name this ruler who in 1902 conquered Riyadh and then went on to consolidate rule over the Nejd and Hedjaz by 1932, displacing the rule of the Rashidi dynasty and establishing a Kingdom since ruled by his sons.
question.answerHtml: (Abdulaziz) Ibn Saud (don’t accept or prompt on Saud because that is his son)

swap.leadin: After bulldozing some berms upon capturing Mosul, ISIS claimed to have ended this agreement.
swap.text: Name this agreement, named for the British and French officials who created it, by which France and the U.K. partitioned the Middle East.
swap.clue: British control over Palestine was decided in this secret 1916 agreement between Britain and France that divided up the territories of the Ottoman Empire.

question.leadin: The organization headed by this man was responsible for the assassination of ambassador Shlomo Argov in London, leading to the 1982 invasion of Lebanon.
question.text: Identify this namesake of a splinter group that rejected the 10 point program of the Palestine Liberation Organization. His nom de guerre translates to "father of the struggle."

swap.leadin: This ruler's sister Fawzia Shirin was the wife of Iran's Mohammad Reza Shah Pahlavi. FTPE.
swap.text: Name this ruler who was overthrown in a 1952 revolution led by Muhammad Naguib and Gamal Abdel Nasser, the final ruling King of Egypt.
swap.clue: To ensure he stayed in power, the CIA pressured this leader into making reforms via the rather aptly named Project Fat Fucker.

question.text: Benny Morris coined this term for a group of Israeli scholars who challenged the traditional narrative among Israeli historians that Palestinian refugees left of their own free will during the Nakba.
question.clue: This collective of Israeli academics which formed in the 1980s and also includes Benny Morris. Its core tenet is that Israel was not being truthful about events such as the Nakba.

swap.leadin: Name these things about a Muslim dynasty, FTP each.
swap.text: The rulers of this Sunnite dynasty included Al-Adil and Al-Kamil, the brother and nephew of its founder Saladin.
swap.clue: This dynasty lost territory under al-Adil and al-Kamil, and was finally driven out of its chief territory following the Battle of al-Mansurah.
